problems.where: S1-O1, contrast 1 (TRIZ-C+LLM vs TRIZ-C, all three problems)
problems.field: contrasts[0].reported and contrasts[0].direction (with statistics_available arm_means_sds_ns and test_statistic)
problems.form_value: Total: TRIZ-C 4.8 (SD 0.90, N 51) vs TRIZ-C+LLM 5.6 (SD 1.13, N 63). Two-way ANOVA (Problem x Method): Method main effect F(1, 108) = 3.21, p = .076, 'which is not significant'; direction no_clear_difference
problems.source_says: Every number is transcribed correctly, but the arm means and the test in this record describe two different comparisons. The Total rows of Table 2 weight each problem by its cell size, and the arms differ in composition: WT, the problem with the highest scores, is 43 of 63 TRIZ-C+LLM students and 30 of 51 TRIZ-C students. The paper never tests the 0.8-point gap between the Total rows. Its Method test is the main effect of a two-way ANOVA with unequal cells. A back-calculation from Table 2 shows which comparison that test covers. The within-cell error variance computed from the Table 2 cell SDs is 0.656 on 108 df. With it, the 0.8-point Total gap gives F = 27.5 (Welch t = 4.2). The per-problem gaps implied by the simple-effect F values are GT -0.25, MB +0.09 and WT +1.13. Their unweighted mean, 0.32, reproduces F = 3.21 (rounded cell means: 4.7 vs 5.0). A cell-size-weighted adjusted gap (0.70) would give F = 21, so the reported test is the unweighted comparison. So 'no_clear_difference' and p = .076 belong to a gap of about 0.3 points between unweighted problem-cell means. A standardized effect computed from the coded arm means would be d = 0.89 with the control SD (0.77 with the pooled SD), and it would carry a p-value and a direction that do not belong to it. one_line_finding repeats the same pairing ('5.6 with TRIZ+LLM vs 4.8 with TRIZ alone (Method main effect F(1, 108) = 3.21, p = .076)'). measure_detail notes the unequal composition but does not say that the test does not compare these means. Fix: keep the three per-problem contrasts as the usable estimates. Then drop the pooled contrast, or record it as the problem-adjusted main effect with the unweighted means (4.7 vs 5.0, derived from Table 2) and a note that the Total rows are not to be used for an effect size.
problems.quote: Regarding the main effect of the Method factor, the following values were obtained: F(1, 108) = 3.21, p = .076, which is not significant. ... Total TRIZ-C 4.8 (4.3) 0.90 (1.44) 51 TRIZ-C+LLM 5.6 (4.7) 1.13 (1.22) 63 (62)
problems.locator: p. 512 (PDF p. 6), Section 4.2 (two-way ANOVA, Method main effect, simple effects) and Table 2 (Total block and the six problem-by-method cells); form one_line_finding and S1-O1 measure_detail

confirmed: S1-O1 is scored on the produced output by raters. Experts holding PhDs in mechanical engineering rated each student's solution on C1 feasibility, C2 requirements, C3 innovativeness and C4 elaboration (1-7), and design quality is the mean of the four. It is not a self-report: the student survey is a separate measure (p. 510-511, PDF pp. 4-5, Sections 3.2.2 and 3.2.3).

Measure expert_raters fits codebook section 6. For GT and MB, two experts with prior experience in the problem domains, not involved in this design problem, rated independently and their scores were averaged per criterion. For WT, another independent expert rated all solutions (p. 511, PDF p. 5, Section 3.2.2).

measure_detail is right that only the composite is reported and that blinding to condition is not stated. The paper also reports no inter-rater agreement (p. 511-512, PDF pp. 5-6, Section 3.2.2, Section 4.2, Table 2).

ai_available_when_produced 'yes' and timing 'immediate' hold. In the same test of about 45 minutes, the TRIZ-C+LLM arm used the LLM to search for contradictions and for specific solutions, then developed and documented its top-ranked idea. The paper never says the LLM was withdrawn, and Figure 3 labels only the TRIZ-C development step 'Manual' (p. 511, PDF p. 5, Section 3.3 and Figure 3).

The rated output comes from the test session. Figures 2 and 3 place the expert evaluation right after the test, although the GT and MB students continued the problem in their course afterward (p. 510, PDF p. 4, Section 3.2.1 and Figure 2; p. 511, Figure 3).
Question 'with_ai' follows the codebook rule: AI was available while the output was produced, and the construct is not diversity (codebook section 1; p. 511, PDF p. 5, Section 3.3).

Construct 'usefulness' is supported. The paper names the composite design quality (RQ1), and codebook section 6 lists quality and feasibility under usefulness. Innovativeness (C3) and elaboration (C4) make up half of the composite and are not reported separately, as measure_detail and open_questions state (p. 508, PDF p. 2, RQ1; p. 510, PDF p. 4, criteria; p. 512, Table 2).

No diversity or flexibility outcome exists. The paper measures no similarity across students and no count of categories within one student. The prompt pack's 'diversity check' is an instruction to the LLM arm, not a measured outcome (p. 511, PDF p. 5, Section 3.3).

Unit 'participant' and n_units 114 match the paper's analysis. Each student developed one top-ranked idea, and the two-way ANOVA has error df 108, which is 114 students minus 6 cells (p. 511, PDF p. 5, Section 3.3; p. 512, PDF p. 6, Section 4.2 and Table 2).

The directions of the three per-problem contrasts follow the paper's simple-effect tests: GT and MB not significant, WT significant with TRIZ-C+LLM higher (p. 512, PDF p. 6, Section 4.2; p. 513-514, PDF pp. 7-8, Discussion).
Primary 'paper_primary' holds: design quality is the outcome of RQ1 (p. 508, PDF p. 2, Section 1).

Comparison type 'ai_vs_bau' holds for all four contrasts. Both arms used the TRIZ contradiction matrix, and the TRIZ-C arm had the triz40.com site and was asked not to use any LLM-based AI assistant (p. 511, PDF p. 5, Section 3.3).

No outcome that bears on the three questions is missing. Every other contrast in the paper is a self-report from the post-experimental survey (workload, perceived usefulness, satisfaction with results, idea quality, innovation gain, feasibility perception, enjoyment) or task completion time. The separate expert criteria are not reported, and no outcome is produced after AI is removed or at a later session (pp. 511-513, PDF pp. 5-7, Sections 3.2.3 and 4.3, Figure 4).
summary: S1-O1, expert-rated design quality of each student's final solution, is scored on the produced output with the LLM available in the treatment arm, and its question (with_ai), measure (expert_raters), unit (participant), per-problem numbers and directions match the paper, with usefulness a defensible construct for the composite. The coding is refuted on one point: the pooled contrast pairs the Table 2 Total means (4.8 vs 5.6, weighted by unequal problem shares) with the ANOVA Method test (F(1, 108) = 3.21, p = .076) and 'no_clear_difference', yet that test matches a gap of about 0.3 points between unweighted problem-cell means, while the 0.8-point Total gap would give F of about 27.5, so an effect size computed from the coded arm means would carry the wrong test and direction.
